title: Rivera v. Meridian Tower Holdings
premise: A college student in a high-rise luxury tower in Manhattan claims constructive eviction due to chronic, unrepaired water leaks that have destroyed their electronics and personal property.

side_A.role: an organiser with a tenants' union
side_A.goal: supporting the tenant against an unfair eviction

side_B.goal: justifying the eviction on grounds of lease violations

=== DOCUMENT 2: Witness Statement of Elena Rivera (Tenant) ===

I am Elena Rivera, the tenant of Unit 402 at 1200 Meridian Plaza. I have lived in this apartment since January 2023. I am writing this statement to detail the horrific conditions I have been forced to endure due to the gross negligence of Meridian Tower Holdings.

When I first signed the lease on January 15, 2023, I was told the building was well-maintained. That was a lie. The building is a 30-story structure built in 1985, and it is crumbling. On March 3, 2024, I reported a leak in my bathroom ceiling through the building app. I expected a quick fix. Instead, Marcus Thorne, the property manager, logged it as "Priority Low." That was the first sign that they didn't care about my safety.

Over the next two months, I submitted a total of 47 maintenance requests. Forty-seven times I asked for help. They ignored me. My apartment became a swamp. The water damage rendered the apartment uninhabitable. Mold covered 80% of the bedroom walls. It was black, fuzzy, and spreading. My medical records show that in April 2024, I was diagnosed with chronic anxiety triggered by this mold exposure. I couldn't breathe. I couldn't sleep.

On May 25, 2024, I received a repair bill for $1,450 for my laptop, which was destroyed by water intrusion. My electronics were destroyed by water dripping directly from the ceiling leak. I kept them on my desk, away from the bathroom, but the ceiling leaked everywhere.

By May 15, 2024, the conditions were so bad that I could no longer stay in the unit. I have slept in my car for 14 nights between May 15 and June 1, 2024. It is cold, and it is humiliating, but at least I am not breathing in mold spores.

On June 1, 2024, I received a formal notice of non-payment from your client. They are citing a $250 late fee for May rent. This is a setup. I stopped paying rent in protest of the living conditions, as I stated in my email to the tenants' union on May 10, 2024. This eviction notice is not about money; it is about punishing me for speaking out. They are trying to drive me out because I joined the tenants' union. This is retaliatory.

I am ready to testify to the fact that my home was destroyed by their inaction.

=== DOCUMENT 3: Witness Statement of Marcus Thorne (Property Manager) ===

My name is Marcus Thorne, and I am the Property Manager for 1200 Meridian Plaza. I have managed this building for five years. I am providing this statement to clarify the facts regarding the maintenance of Unit 402.

Ms. Rivera’s lease, signed on January 15, 2023, is a standard residential agreement. It explicitly states that the tenant is responsible for minor cosmetic repairs under $100, such as patching minor paint chips. While this does not cover structural leaks, it establishes that Ms. Rivera is expected to maintain the interior of her unit to a reasonable standard.

On March 3, 2024, at 14:02, I logged Ms. Rivera’s initial complaint regarding a bathroom ceiling leak. I assigned it a priority of "Low" because, at that time, it appeared to be a minor drip from a single supply line, not a structural failure. We do not treat every drip as an emergency.

Contrary to Ms. Rivera’s claims, we did not ignore her. On March 15, 2024, a licensed plumber visited Unit 402 for 45 minutes. We dispatched this technician within 48 hours of the first complaint to fix the leak. The plumber replaced a gasket, and we billed $800 for parts and labor, as documented in our records. This was a timely and professional response.

Ms. Rivera claims that mold covered 80% of her bedroom walls and that the apartment was uninhabitable. This is false. The water damage was localized to a single ceiling tile in the bathroom. No mold was present in the bedroom. The building’s fire safety inspection report from January 2024 noted "minor moisture" in the basement utility room, which is unrelated to Unit 402, but this shows that we monitor moisture issues in the building. We did not see extensive mold in Unit 402 during our inspections.

Regarding the damage to Ms. Rivera’s electronics, she claims the water dripped from the ceiling. My assessment is that the electronics were damaged due to the tenant's failure to move them away from the window where rain entered. The window seals in Unit 402 are old, and it is the tenant's responsibility to ensure that personal property is not placed in areas susceptible to weather intrusion. She has not provided evidence that the ceiling leak reached her desk.

Finally, regarding the eviction notice issued on June 1, 2024: This was issued solely because Rivera failed to pay the $250 late fee on time. The rent for Unit 402 is $4,500 per month. She did not pay the late fee. We follow the lease terms. There is no retaliation. The "quiet enjoyment" clause in her lease protects her right to use the apartment, but it does not exempt her from paying her rent.

=== DOCUMENT 4: Witness Statement of Chloe Diaz (Tenants' Union Organizer) ===

I am Chloe Diaz, an organizer for the Tenants' Union. I have been working with Ms. Rivera since March 2024. I am familiar with the conditions in Unit 402 and the management practices of Meridian Tower Holdings.

Ms. Rivera is a victim of a systemic failure by the landlord. The landlord never attempted to repair the leak, ignoring all requests for over two months. While they sent a plumber once in March, it was a token gesture. They did not fix the root cause. The leak continued. Ms. Rivera submitted 47 maintenance requests. Forty-seven! And they kept logging them as "Low Priority." This is not maintenance; this is neglect.

The living conditions in Unit 402 became dangerous. Ms. Rivera’s medical records show she developed chronic anxiety in April 2024 due to mold exposure. This is not a minor issue. The mold was pervasive. The landlord knew about it. Their board meeting minutes from March 20, 2024, list "Unit 402 leak" as a recurring agenda item requiring budget approval. They had the funds. They chose not to spend them.

On May 10, 2024, Ms. Rivera sent an email to our union stating that she had stopped paying rent in protest of the living conditions. This was a calculated decision to draw attention to the uninhabitable state of her home. When the landlord issued a notice of non-payment on June 1, 2024, citing a $250 late fee, it was clearly retaliatory. The eviction notice was issued in retaliation for Rivera's participation in the tenants' union. They are trying to break her by using the legal system.

The property loss is also a result of their negligence. Ms. Rivera’s laptop was destroyed by the water. The landlord’s claim that rain entered through the window is a deflection. The primary issue was the ceiling leak. The water was coming from above. The landlord’s insurance policy has a deductible of $2,500 per claim for water damage, which suggests they view water damage as a frequent, manageable cost rather than a critical hazard.

Ms. Rivera has slept in her car for 14 nights between May 15 and June 1, 2024. This is because her home was unsafe. We demand that the landlord pay for the repairs and the damages, or they will face legal consequences for their negligence.

=== DOCUMENT 5: Witness Statement of Sarah Jenkins (Landlord Counsel) ===

I am Sarah Jenkins, counsel for Meridian Tower Holdings. I am submitting this statement on behalf of my client.

The facts in this case are straightforward. Ms. Rivera is in default of her lease agreement. The lease, dated January 15, 2023, requires timely payment of rent. Ms. Rivera failed to pay the $250 late fee for May 2024. On June 1, 2024, we issued a formal notice of non-payment. This is a standard legal procedure. It is not retaliatory.

Ms. Rivera’s claims of "uninhabitable" conditions are exaggerated. The building is a 30-story structure from 1985. It is a well-maintained building. The leak in Unit 402 was addressed. On March 15, 2024, a licensed plumber visited the unit for 45 minutes. We dispatched a licensed plumber within 48 hours of the first complaint to fix the leak. The maintenance invoice for $800 in parts and labor proves that we acted.

Ms. Rivera’s claim that the landlord ignored her for two months is false. We received 47 tickets, but many were duplicates or complaints about the same minor issue. We did not have the resources to send a plumber every time she complained about a drip. However, we did send one.

Regarding the mold, Ms. Rivera claims 80% of her bedroom walls were covered. This is not supported by our inspections. The water damage was localized to a single ceiling tile. No mold was present in the bedroom. The fire safety inspection report from January 2024 noted minor moisture in the basement, but that is unrelated to Unit 402. There is no evidence of widespread mold in Ms. Rivera’s bedroom.

The damage to her laptop is not our responsibility. The lease states that the tenant is responsible for minor repairs and the care of their personal property. The electronics were damaged due to the tenant's failure to move them away from the window where rain entered. It is not the landlord's fault if the tenant leaves electronics near a window in a building from 1985.

The utility bill showing a 40% increase in water usage for the building in April 2024 compared to April 2023 is a building-wide metric. It does not prove that Unit 402 had a major leak. It could be due to other factors, such as increased occupancy or landscaping.

Ms. Rivera’s rent of $4,500 per month is 15% below the average rent for comparable units in the building. She is receiving a discount. She is not being treated unfairly. She is simply not paying her bills. We will enforce the lease.
